display.purpose: Hero claims, section titles, and markdown headings only — never body chrome, never bolded.

mono.purpose: The workhorse voice: chrome, labels, buttons, tables, terminal text, and tabular numerals.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: The only elevation shadow family in the system — dropdown panes, tooltip bubbles, the hero terminal, toasts, and the command palette. Never applied to ordinary content.

shadows.name: focus-ring-accent
shadows.purpose: Universal focus-visible treatment on interactive controls.

shadows.name: focus-ring-error
shadows.purpose: Focus/validation ring on a field in an error state.

shadows.name: liveness-glow-accent
shadows.value: 0 0 0 0 color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, transparent) -> 0 0 0 5px transparent, 1.6-2.4s cycle
shadows.purpose: Pulsing ring signaling 'this is live right now' — a running pipeline node, a live status dot. Never a substitute for overlay-lift.

shadows.name: liveness-glow-money
shadows.value: 0 0 9px color-mix(in srgb, var(--up) or var(--down) 44%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: Soft glow on a live status dot tied to a gain/loss read.

motion.name: ease-house
motion.purpose: The single default easing curve for nearly every transition in the system — progressively enhanced to a matching linear() spring under @supports.

motion.name: duration-hover
motion.purpose: Micro hover transitions on chips, tabs, borders, buttons.

motion.name: cursor-blink
motion.purpose: The terminal/streaming cursor's hard binary blink — no fade, reads as an authentic terminal caret.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single solid-fill accent action allowed per viewport.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.78rem; letter-spacing: 0.02em; background: var(--accent); color: #06110f; border: 1px solid var(--accent); border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.62rem 1.3rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 3px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The default choice for any non-primary action.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.78rem; letter-spacing: 0.02em; background: transparent; color: var(--ink); border: 1px solid var(--hair); border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.62rem 1.3rem; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.2s var(--ease); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 50%, var(--hair)); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 3px; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive action — outline only, fills faintly on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.78rem; letter-spacing: 0.02em; background: transparent; color: var(--down); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--down) 40%, var(--hair)); border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.62rem 1.3rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s var(--ease); } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--down) 10%, transparent); }

components.name: Card
components.description: The universal flat container — hairline border is the only depth cue.
components.html:
Positions

Flat panel, hairline border, no shadow.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--hair); border-radius: 12px; padding: 1.2rem; transition: border-color 0.2s var(--ease); } .ds-card:hover { border-color: var(--hair-2); } .ds-card-title { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.95rem; color: var(--ink); margin: 0 0 0.4rem; } .ds-card-body { font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.85rem; color: var(--ink-soft); margin: 0; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Text field — reads as canvas cut into the surrounding surface.
components.css: .ds-input { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--ink); background: var(--bg); border: 1px solid var(--hair); border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.55rem 0.7rem; width: 100%; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--ink-mute); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, var(--hair)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 22%, transparent); } .ds-input[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color: var(--down); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--down) 20%, transparent); }

components.name: Selected Chip
components.description: The system's signature selection grammar — used for livery, tabs, and segmented controls alike.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.4rem; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.7rem; letter-spacing: 0.04em; background: var(--surface); color: var(--ink-soft); border: 1px solid var(--hair); border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.4rem 0.75rem; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.2s var(--ease), color 0.2s var(--ease), background-color 0.2s var(--ease); } .ds-chip--on { color: var(--ink); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, var(--hair)); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 12%, var(--surface)); } .ds-chip-dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--accent); box-shadow: 0 0 8px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Badge
components.description: Outlined semantic pill — color reserved for meaning, never decoration.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-block; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.7rem; border: 1px solid var(--hair); border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.16rem 0.5rem; color: var(--ink-mute); } .ds-badge--up { color: var(--up); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--up) 40%, var(--hair)); } .ds-badge--down { color: var(--down); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--down) 40%, var(--hair)); } .ds-badge--warn { color: var(--warn); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--warn) 40%, var(--hair)); }

narrative.overview:
digiweb reads as a cockpit, not a brochure. Monochrome is the resting state — black, white, and a three-step ink hierarchy — with color held in reserve as a signal, never spent as decoration. Every affordance from a button to a candlestick chart is built out of the same restrained kit: hairline borders, pill controls, one mono type voice for anything that is chrome or data, and a single serif voice reserved for the moments the product actually wants to make a human claim. The system does not perform enthusiasm; it reports state precisely and gets out of the way.

That restraint is structural, not stylistic. A dashboard, a landing page, and a terminal-style chatbot all draw from the same instrument-panel vocabulary — the module color that dresses digigraph's marketing hero is the identical --accent variable a digiquant chart reads to tint its equity line, just scoped differently. Color is a wiring diagram, not a moodboard: every hue in the system routes to an explicit meaning (a module's identity, a gain, a loss, a diff) and never means two things in the same place.

digiweb explicitly rejects the AI-slop default aesthetic: no purple-to-blue gradient heroes, no glassmorphism, no floating gradient blobs, no Inter-as-brand-font, no decorative box-shadow lifted off nothing in particular. Depth comes from hairline borders and tonal layering; when a shadow does appear, it means something specific.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome-by-default livery; color is opt-in per surface and always routes through --accent, never a hardcoded hex.

Three color domains that never blend: identity (--accent / module liveries), money (--up / --down, fixed literals, livery-proof), and diff (--rv-add / --rv-del, a third pastel-only palette reserved for code review).
One mono voice for chrome and data, one serif voice for the rare human claim — never both competing on the same element.
Pill shape means 'you can act on this'; rectangular 8–16px radius means 'this is a container.'
'One loud thing per viewport': exactly one solid-fill, accent-colored control is allowed on screen at a time.
Flat by default; a black shadow means 'this is a floating overlay,' an accent glow means 'this is alive right now.'

rules.name: The One-Livery Rule
rules.body: Exactly one module accent is active at a time, set via a global livery switcher or a local .accent-<module> scope class — never two module hues visible in the same view. atlas/hermes/kairos collapse to plain --ink since they name backend LangGraphs, not colored products.

rules.name: The Ledger Rule
rules.body: Gain/Loss are fixed to their own token or a bare literal — never var(--accent) — so a livery switch or theme flip can never repaint a P&L number.

rules.name: The Three Domains Rule
rules.body: Identity, Money, and Diff are three separate color systems that must never blend into one palette or substitute for each other, even where a hue coincidentally matches.

rules.name: The Terminal-Ink Rule
rules.body: The Terminal component family carries its own always-dark-feeling palette, resolved independently of the page's own theme — a terminal reads as a terminal even inside a light-themed page.

rules.name: The Normative Display Rule
rules.body: tokens.css sets --font-display to Instrument Serif — this is what digithings.ai, digiquant.io, digichat, and olympus actually ship. Fraunces is a design-reference demo furnishing only, never the production default.

rules.name: The Mono-First Rule
rules.body: Serif is for marketing hero display and rare human-identity moments only. Dashboards, data, and chrome are set in sans + mono — never serif.

rules.name: The One Glyph, One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Five distinct prompt/marker glyphs ($ ❯ > ▸ ·) exist across the system and are never reused across registers — each glyph alone tells you which surface you're in.

rules.name: The Command-Band-Then-Ledger Rule
rules.body: Every dashboard surface composes the same way: one restrained command band naming the primary state, followed by a single full-width hairline ledger table. Never a stack of nested decorative cards.

rules.name: The Crop-Never-Break Rule
rules.body: Product screenshots inside a ProductFrame scale down to fit their container but never scale up past their authored size — an undersized container crops rather than reflowing.

rules.name: The Overlay-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: If a component is not a dropdown, tooltip, toast, command palette, or the hero terminal, it does not get a drop shadow.

rules.name: The Shape-Carries-Meaning Rule
rules.body: Do not use a pill for a container or a rectangular radius for a clickable control — the distinction is load-bearing across the whole system.

dos: Do build under the [data-theme]-scoped token system (--bg / --surface / --ink family, --r-sm/md/lg = 8/12/16px) — this is the normative, currently-shipping scale.
Do treat Instrument Serif as the production display font; treat any Fraunces sighting as reference-app furniture, not a target to copy.
Do keep money colors (--up/--down/--warn) fixed to their own token or literal, never var(--accent) — a livery switch must never repaint a P&L number.
Do give every interactive control the same focus recipe: outline: none plus a 2–4px color-mix(var(--accent) or var(--down), ~50%, transparent) box-shadow ring.
Do reserve solid, filled-accent surfaces for exactly one control per viewport; every sibling control should be a transparent, hairline-bordered outline.
Do use the five scoped prompt/marker glyphs ($ ❯ > ▸ ·) exactly as documented — never invent a sixth or reuse one across registers.
Do keep buy-side/positive-chrome markers on --accent and sell-side/negative markers on --down in the tearsheet/finance charting family — the split is deliberate.
donts: Don't mix the legacy unscoped :root token system (--radius-sm/md/lg = 6/8/12px, --space-1..9, Inter as --font-family) into new work — it serves un-migrated legacy pages only.
Don't apply a box-shadow to ordinary content (cards, panels, dashboard composites). If it isn't a dropdown, tooltip, toast, command palette, or the hero terminal, it stays flat.
Don't color two different module liveries in the same view — the system is strictly one-livery-at-a-time.
Don't let atlas, hermes, or kairos render as colored products on a redesigned surface — they name backend LangGraph sub-graphs and must collapse to plain ink.
Don't reuse the diff palette (--rv-add/--rv-del) for anything except unified-diff review UI, and don't reuse money colors for a non-financial positive/negative read.
Don't put a message in a bubble or box inside the chat transcript — plain turns are grid rows; only rich embedded objects earn a frame.

Don't carry forward the reference implementation's remaining known gaps (missing :disabled styling on ghost/quiet/danger buttons, digichat's light-theme accent contrast failure) as if they were intentional patterns. (The undeclared --surface-inverse fallback was fixed — every consumer now routes through the already-correct --on-accent token.)
